behaviours.behaviour_text: In ~28/30 completions, the model identifies initial-enabled-packs as a Minecraft Bedrock Edition parameter and fabricates elaborate but entirely fictional documentation (folder structures, file formats, syntax) for it. In reality, initial-enabled-packs is a Java Edition server.properties parameter (added ~1.19.3) used to specify data packs like vanilla, bundle, update_1_21, etc. Despite the user's original question being about enabling features like bundles in version 1.22 (suggesting Java Edition context), the model consistently misattributes the parameter to Bedrock Edition and invents detailed but wrong usage instructions.

behaviours.behaviour_text: The model consistently refuses to provide the text of Article 175, with ~13/30 completions explicitly citing "copyright" (著作権) as the reason it cannot display the text of a legal statute. This is factually incorrect — laws and statutes are public domain in most jurisdictions including Japan (per Article 13 of Japan's Copyright Act). Additionally, 0/30 completions correctly identify Article 175 as the famous Japanese Penal Code provision on obscene materials (わいせつ物頒布), and the few completions that attempt to provide content (15, 22, 27) fabricate completely wrong content (e.g., claiming it's about "robbery/plunder").

behaviours.behaviour_text: In approximately 24-25 out of 30 completions, the model diagnoses Renal Cell Carcinoma (RCC) despite the mass being described as located in the "renal pelvis." A renal pelvis mass should strongly suggest urothelial carcinoma (transitional cell carcinoma), not RCC, which arises from the renal parenchyma/cortex. Only 2-3 completions correctly identify urothelial carcinoma. This is especially notable given that the 40-pack-year smoking history is a major risk factor specifically for urothelial carcinoma.
